title: Two settings pages disagree about whether a filter wheel exists; per-filter adaptive-exposure limits become unreachable
summary: The per-filter editor read only activeEquipmentProfileProvider?.filterNames, so a connected wheel with no filters saved on the profile produced the false banner 'No filter wheel on active profile' while Autofocus (which reads the live wheel) listed all seven. It now watches effectiveFiltersProvider - the shared source of truth already used by capture_settings_panel, plan_tonight and session_optimizer (connected wheel names, else profile names, with generic slot labels falling back to profile names). The implicit 'all filters enabled' materialization in the checkbox handler was reading the profile list too, so unticking one filter would have disabled every wheel-only filter; it now materializes over the same effective list. The banner copy now names both missing sources instead of asserting a false one.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/adaptive_exposure_filter_source_test.dart (3 tests): connected wheel supplies the rows when the profile has none; the warning names both missing sources; per-filter enablement materializes over the effective filters.
revert_check: Reverted adaptive_exposure_settings.dart:316 from `final filterNames = ref.watch(effectiveFiltersProvider);` back to `final filterNames = ref.watch(activeEquipmentProfileProvider)?.filterNames ?? const <String>[];` -> 2 of 3 tests fail (rows never appear, enablement map is empty). Restored -> 5/5 pass including the pre-existing adaptive_exposure_settings_test.dart.
caveats: The verifier's note that per-filter limits are wholly unreachable was already overstated (Edit Profile > Filters > Auto-detect from wheel > Save was a workaround). This removes the need for that workaround.

title: 'Auto dark subtraction' in Dark Library is the same switch as 'Auto-calibrate light frames'
summary: Confirmed one boolean (calibration.auto_calibrate) behind two contradictory labels. The Dark Library row now carries the Calibration page's title and subtitle verbatim ('Auto-calibrate light frames' / 'Apply dark, flat, and bias correction to captured images automatically. Same setting as Settings > Calibration.') so the control cannot understate what one tap disables. A load-bearing comment records that this switch gates the entire calibrateFile() call.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/dark_library_auto_calibrate_label_test.dart (2 tests): the row is labelled for everything the switch actually gates (asserts the new copy AND that the old darks-only copy is gone); toggling it writes the shared master calibration flag (drives the real switch and asserts calibrationSettingsProvider.autoCalibrate flips to false and the DB row calibration.auto_calibrate becomes 'false').
revert_check: Restored the old title/subtitle at dark_library_settings.dart:88-90 ('Auto dark subtraction' / 'Automatically subtract matching darks from light frames') -> both tests fail. Restored -> 3/3 pass including the pre-existing dark_library_dialog_authority_test.dart.
needs_shared_change: The remaining half of the finding's 'expected' -- letting a user run darks off with flats on -- needs a per-frame-type gate that does not exist: CalibrationSettings has a single autoCalibrate, and packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/imaging_service.dart gates the whole calibrateFile() call on it (the call returns darkApplied/flatApplied/biasApplied but is never entered when the flag is false). Splitting it means new settings keys (calibration.auto_dark/auto_flat/auto_bias), a CalibrationSettings model change, and passing the per-type flags into calibrateFile -- all in skotiq_core, outside this agent's ownership. Filed rather than faked.
caveats: This closes the false-label defect, not the missing per-frame-type control (see needs_shared_change).

title: File naming pattern accepts unknown variables and path-traversal segments with no validation
summary: Added packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/imaging_naming_pattern.dart: checkNamingPattern() applies the capture pipeline's own rules (the full $TOKEN set including the $EXPOSURE/$SEQ aliases, relative-path rule, residual-'$' rule, and the empty/'.'/'..'/backslash/unsafe-char segment rules) and renders the example path the pattern resolves to. imaging_settings.dart now commits through _commitPattern, which throws on an invalid pattern so SettingsTextInput rolls the field back to the stored value, and shows either the rejection reason or 'Example: M31/light/M31_L_0001.fits' under the row. The token set had to be mirrored because ImagingService._patternVariables is private and the entry points are @visibleForTesting; the drift risk is covered by a test that runs an 18-pattern corpus through BOTH implementations and asserts identical accept/reject plus an identical rendered path.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/imaging_naming_pattern_test.dart (24 tests): 18 accept/reject parity cases against ImagingService.buildImageFilePath; 'the preview is the path the pipeline would actually write'; 'every token the pipeline knows is offered by the validator'; plus 4 widget tests that type into the real field and assert the DB row is unchanged for a bad pattern, updated for a good one, and that a pattern already persisted before this validation existed is reported instead of sitting silently.
revert_check: Replaced `onChanged: _commitPattern,` at imaging_settings.dart:137 with the original direct `ref.read(appSettingsProvider.notifier).setFileNamingPattern(value)` -- i.e. cut the production call site, leaving the validator itself intact -> the 2 rejection widget tests fail (the bad pattern reaches the DB and no error renders). Restored -> 23/23 pass.
caveats: The finding's 'path-traversal' framing was already corrected by the verifier: buildImageFilePath rejects '..' and enforces path.isWithin, so nothing escaped the output root. This was a deferred-error validation gap, and that is what is fixed.

title: Adaptive Conditions accepts all-zero score weights and calls it a readability preference
summary: Both halves fixed. (1) _setWeight now computes the prospective total before writing and throws when it would be <= 0, so zeroing the LAST non-zero weight is refused, the number field rolls back to the stored value, and an error names the consequence. Zeroing any other weight is still allowed. _WeightRow.onChanged was widened from ValueChanged<double> (void) to Future<void> Function(double) -- with the void signature the rejection would have been swallowed and the field would have kept showing an unsaved 0. (2) The callout now has a distinct zero branch, because an all-zero map is still reachable from an older DB, a remote host or a hand-edited row; it says no score can be computed and swapping will not run, instead of the false 'the composer renormalizes available axes at runtime'.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/adaptive_conditions_zero_weights_test.dart (3 tests): zeroing the last non-zero weight is refused and neither the provider nor the adaptive_swap.score_weights DB row changes; zeroing a weight that leaves a non-zero total still saves (guards against over-clamping); an already-zero total is described truthfully.
revert_check: Two separate reverts. (a) Deleted the `if (total <= 0) { ... throw ArgumentError.value(...); }` block in _setWeight -> 'zeroing the last non-zero weight is refused, not saved' fails (the 0 lands in the DB, no error renders). (b) Restored the callout to branch on `nearOne` only -> 'an already-zero total is described truthfully' fails on the 'renormalizes available axes' copy. Restored -> 5/5 pass including the pre-existing adaptive_conditions_settings_test.dart.
caveats: The Rust-side guard (adaptive_swap_service.dart:174 `if (weightTotal <= 0) return null;`) is deliberately left alone -- it is the correct defensive behaviour for a state this UI can no longer create.

title: Sequence checkpoints and logs are written to the platform app-support directory, ignoring the configured data directory
summary: Confirmed the verifier's corrected location, not the reporter's ('the native bridge startup path'). Both writes are Dart and both bypass SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 calls backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir(supportDir.path) with getApplicationSupportDirectory(), and apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60-68 builds logDir from the same call. configureSkotiqDataDirectory (desktop_logging_init.dart:31-37) only *fills* SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when it is unset and is never consulted by either path, so an operator-supplied data dir is silently ignored and a GUI + headless daemon on one host share one skotiq_session.checkpoint. Both files are outside this agent's ownership (settings widgets only) and are plausibly being edited concurrently, so no change was made.
test: None written -- the fix belongs in files this agent does not own.
needs_shared_change: Add a single resolver (e.g. `Future<Directory> resolveSkotiqDataRoot()` next to configureSkotiqDataDirectory) that returns SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when set and getApplicationSupportDirectory() otherwise, then use it in BOTH apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60 (logDir = <root>/logs) and packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 (sequencerSetCheckpointDir(<root>)). Note the ordering constraint: configureSkotiqDataDirectory currently runs before the resolver would, and app_shell reads the env var in a different isolate-visible process env, so the resolver must read Platform.environment rather than caching the value set by _setProcessEnvironment.
caveats: Reproduced by inspection only in this session; the live evidence is the verifier's (/proc environ vs the instance's own 'Log directory:' / 'Setting checkpoint directory to:' log lines, plus a phantom 'Recover Sequence?' dialog for a run absent from that profile's sequence_checkpoints table).
